entry.title: FCA proposes exempting performance fees from workplace pension default fund charge cap
entry.summary: FCA proposes greater pension investment flexibility to support long-term value for savers FCA · Nov 12, 2026 · Draft / consultationThe FCA is consulting on excluding certain performance-linked fees from the charge cap for default funds in workplace pensions, giving providers more flexibility to invest in private markets for long-term returns. The proposals include safeguards on transparency, fair allocation of fees between savers, and scrutiny of how private assets are valued. The consultation closes on 14 January 2027, and the FCA expects to make final rules in summer 2027.

entry.title: Man sentenced for fake £154m takeover bid targeting UK-listed company
entry.summary: Man sentenced over £154m fake takeover bid targeting UK-listed company FCA · Nov 10, 2026 · EnforcementThe FCA announced that Christopher Woolcott received a 2-year prison sentence, suspended for 2 years, plus 200 hours of unpaid work and costs for staging a fake takeover bid for Touchstone Exploration Inc. He invented several identities, forged takeover documents and met the chief executive under a false name. The aim was to drive up the share price and profit from selling his shares.

entry.title: Start your Self Assessment tax return early before the 31 January deadline
entry.summary: Stay on top of your finances, start your Self Assessment today HMRC / gov.uk · Nov 10, 2026 · GuidanceHMRC encourages Self Assessment customers to start their tax return for the 2025 to 2026 tax year now, as the filing and payment deadline is 31 January 2027. Returns can be filed and tax paid online via GOV.UK or the HMRC app. The notice also says UK cryptoasset owners must pay Capital Gains Tax on gains above the £3,000 allowance and declare them in their Self Assessment return.</summary>

entry.title: The Not-So-Fine Print: How the FCA Makes Consumer Contracts Fair
entry.summary: The not-so-fine print: making consumer contracts fair FCA · Nov 6, 2026 · Guidance · CryptoTopic evidence: 「A crypto firm agreed to stop charging excessive storage fees which, in some cases, could exceed £40,000 a year.」 The UK Financial Conduct Authority explains how it checks whether terms in financial consumer contracts are fair and transparent under the Consumer Rights Act 2015. It gives examples including a crypto firm that stopped excessive storage fees, an adviser that dropped a complaint-handling charge, and a travel insurer that clarified unclear delay terms. It sets out what firms should do, such as using plain language and reviewing contracts regularly.

entry.title: FCA acts to protect consumers facing repayment demands on disguised remuneration scheme loans
entry.summary: FCA acts to protect consumers facing demands for disguised remuneration scheme loan repayments FCA · Nov 5, 2026 · EnforcementAfter FCA intervention, Ethica Resolve Limited, an FCA-authorised debt collection firm, agreed to restrictions. It had demanded repayment of disguised remuneration loans, or purported loans, on behalf of West 28th Street Limited, which bought them from a third party. Under the agreed requirements, Ethica will tell affected consumers they have no enforceable payment obligation for now, will make no further payment demands in the proposed court claim, and will not seek default judgments.

entry.title: UK-Switzerland Financial Dialogue 2026 joint statement
entry.summary: UK-Switzerland Financial Dialogue 2026 Joint Statement HMRC / gov.uk · Nov 5, 2026A joint statement by HM Treasury and Switzerland's State Secretariat for International Finance on the 2026 UK-Switzerland Financial Dialogue. The dialogue was held on Wednesday 4 November 2026. The statement summarises the meeting's discussions and key outcomes.

entry.title: UK FCA to set up quantum computing group to explore tackling financial crime
entry.summary: FCA to explore quantum computing to tackle financial crime FCA · Nov 5, 2026The UK Financial Conduct Authority will bring together financial firms, quantum technology providers and national research laboratories in a Quantum Experimentation Group. The group will initially explore how quantum machine learning could help detect money laundering and fraud, using an FCA synthetic dataset. It is due to launch in the first quarter of 2027, and organisations can register interest by 31 December 2026.

entry.title: Looking back to move forward: why reviewing rules matters
entry.summary: Looking back to move forward: why reviewing our rules matters FCA · Nov 5, 2026 · GuidanceThe FCA explains why it regularly reviews its rules as markets, consumer behaviour and technology change. It describes its Rule Review Framework, which uses evidence assessments, post-implementation reviews and impact evaluations. Examples include mortgage rule changes, Senior Managers and Certification Regime reforms, wholesale transaction-reporting changes and IPO research rules.

entry.title: Preparing for the quantum future: UK FCA urges financial firms to start post-quantum cryptography migration now
entry.summary: Act now to be resilient in the quantum future FCA · Nov 4, 2026 · GuidanceThe UK Financial Conduct Authority says a viable quantum computer could break widely used cryptography, so firms should prepare now for post-quantum cryptography (PQC). It cites National Cyber Security Centre milestones: a migration plan by 2028, high-priority migration by 2031, and all systems migrated by 2035. The notice also attaches a G7 Cyber Expert Group statement offering a non-binding roadmap for the transition. entry.title: FCA sets rules for car finance settlement offers during legal challenges
entry.summary: FCA sets expectations for firms making car finance settlement offers FCA · Nov 3, 2026 · GuidanceThe UK Financial Conduct Authority sets expectations for lenders making settlement offers to customers owed compensation under its motor finance scheme while legal challenges continue. Offers must be no less than what the scheme would pay. Accepting an offer is full and final, and cannot be referred to the Financial Ombudsman Service.

entry.title: UK regulator brings ESG rating providers under FCA rules for the first time
entry.summary: New FCA rules bring ESG rating providers into UK regulation for the first time FCA · Nov 3, 2026 · RuleThe FCA has published final rules (PS26/22) creating a regulatory regime for ESG rating providers. The framework aims to improve transparency, reliability and comparability of ESG ratings used in investment decisions. Providers must apply for FCA authorisation from 24 June 2027, and the regime takes effect on 29 June 2028.

entry.title: Demands for disguised remuneration scheme loan repayments
entry.summary: Demands for disguised remuneration scheme loan repayments FCA · Nov 2, 2026 · GuidanceThe FCA has seen demands for repayment of loans, or purported loans, provided under disguised remuneration schemes. Some affected people dispute the amounts claimed and whether the debts can be legally enforced. The FCA urges recipients to think carefully before paying, review HMRC guidance, consider legal advice, and report any undue pressure to the FCA.

entry.title: FCA publishes terms of reference for independent review of its handling of whistleblower Simon Andriesz
entry.summary: FCA publishes terms of reference for independent review concerning Mr Andriesz FCA · Nov 2, 2026The UK Financial Conduct Authority has published the terms of reference for an independent review of its handling of interactions with whistleblower Simon Andriesz. The review, led by independent non-executive director Lea Paterson CBE, covers at least 2017 to 2026. It will assess whether the FCA met its whistleblowing law responsibilities and its own policies, and will recommend improvements. A progress update is due in January 2027 and a final report in spring 2027.

entry.title: UK adults far better at spotting pressure tactics in horror films than in investment pitches
entry.summary: Brits nearly twice as likely to spot pressure tactics in horror films as investment red flags FCA · Oct 30, 2026 · ReportNew FCA survey data shows UK adults aged 18 to 40 who own or are considering investments are nearly twice as likely to recognise pressure tactics in horror films as when the same tactics promote investments. Respondents were also less sceptical of novelty, peer pressure and hype in investment contexts. The FCA's InvestSmart campaign offers a Hype Type Revealer tool to help people understand what may influence their investment decisions.

entry.title: FCA urges former Verus Financial Services customers to check FSCS compensation eligibility
entry.summary: FCA encourages former Verus Financial Services Limited customers to check if they can claim with FSCS FCA · Oct 29, 2026 · EnforcementFormer customers of Verus Financial Services Limited can now check on the FSCS website whether they may claim compensation, subject to assessment. The FCA supports the FSCS as it assesses claims against the firm and decides whether individual claims are eligible. Verus was an independent adviser on investments, pensions, mortgages, equity release and insurance, and since 2025 it has had no permission to carry out regulated financial services in the UK.

entry.title: UK regulator secures halt to HTX's unlawful crypto promotions
entry.summary: FCA stops HTX's crypto promotions FCA · Oct 29, 2026 · Enforcement · CryptoTopic evidence: 「Crypto firms should be under no illusion: being based overseas does not put them beyond the reach of UK law.」 The FCA reached a High Court settlement with Huobi Global S.A., the company behind crypto exchange HTX (formerly Huobi). It has undertaken not to knowingly promote cryptoasset services to UK consumers in breach of section 21 of FSMA. HTX has exited the UK, with deposits and new sign-ups no longer possible. The settlement terms are confidential and involve no admission of liability.

entry.title: FCA: What 'fair value' looks like in practice three years into the Consumer Duty
entry.summary: What does 'fair value' look like in practice? Three years into the Consumer Duty, here’s what we’ve learned. FCA · Oct 29, 2026 · GuidanceThe FCA reviewed how consumer finance firms assess, evidence and monitor fair value three years into the Consumer Duty, and carried out focused work on fees and charges across credit products and supervisory work on home energy consumer hire agreements. It found that weaker firms relied on assumptions, treated target markets as single groups and did not test customer understanding. The article sets out questions firms can use to challenge their own fair value approaches.

entry.title: Notice that Bullseye Financial Ltd has entered administration
entry.summary: Bullseye Financial Ltd enters administration FCA · Oct 27, 2026 · EnforcementThe FCA reports that Bullseye Financial Ltd entered administration on 23 October 2026, with Robert Young of Azets and Matthew Haw of RSM UK appointed as joint administrators. The firm served only professional investors and had agreed on 11 March 2026 to stop all regulated activity. The notice lists customer contact details and warns the public about fraudsters posing as the firm or its administrators.

entry.title: FCA survey finds firms' satisfaction, confidence and trust in the regulator rising
entry.summary: Firms’ confidence, satisfaction and trust in the FCA rise FCA · Oct 2, 2026 · ReportThe FCA and Practitioner Panel's annual survey of regulated firms reports higher satisfaction, confidence and trust in the FCA, with 79% of firms highly satisfied with their relationship. 88% say they understand the FCA's expectations under the Consumer Duty. Some firms still find regulation burdensome, and the FCA is simplifying reporting requirements.
